questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a required condition for a variable $X$ to have a binomial distribution $B(n, p)$?
choices: The probability of success changes with each trial
There is a fixed number of trials $n$
Each trial results in one of only two outcomes (success or failure)
Trials are independent of one another
questions.answer: In a binomial distribution, the probability of success $p$ must remain strictly constant across all trials.

sections.heading: Section 3: Mean & Variance of the Binomial Distribution

questions.q: A random variable $X \sim B(48, 0.25)$. Find its mean and standard deviation.
questions.answer: Mean $\mu = np = 48(0.25) = 12$. Variance $\sigma^2 = np(1 - p) = 48(0.25)(0.75) = 9$. Standard deviation $\sigma = \sqrt{9} = 3$.

questions.q: For a binomial distribution $X \sim B(n, p)$, the mean is 6 and the variance is 3.6. Find $n$ and $p$.
What is the maximum possible variance of a binomial distribution with $n = 40$ trials?
questions.answer: Variance $= np(1 - p)$. The quadratic $p(1 - p)$ is maximized at $p = 0.5$, giving maximum variance $= 40(0.5)(0.5) = 10$.

questions.q: A treatment is successful for 80% of patients. If 10 patients are treated, what is the most likely number of successful outcomes (the mode)?
questions.answer: The mean is $np = 10(0.8) = 8$. For integer $(n+1)p = 11(0.8) = 8.8$, the mode is the integer part $\lfloor 8.8 \rfloor = 8$.
